scope: PR #182 (~14 files): combinatorial-testing.md + coverage-measure.mjs (t-way coverage) in comprehensive-test-strategy; the oracle rule (SKILL.md Step 6, renumbered) + leak-check.mjs (reference tested oracle); ADR-0095; CHANGELOG; 2 BDD scenarios + step defs + datastore; two test files; package.json. The mechanical gate, the renumber, em-dash, and index checks passed; the review raised five fail-closed / honest-limits findings, all fixed before this entry.

boundary.evidence: a single-purpose coverage measurer, matching the skill's existing check-test-shape.mjs pattern.

ownership.evidence: the combinatorial-coverage measurement has one owner here.

dependency.evidence: Node built-ins only (node:fs); no outbound web.

error-handling.evidence: fail-closed on a bad plan, undeclared row value, strength out of range, non-integer strength, zero rows/factors, total==0. F1 fix: the coverage key is type-preserving (JSON.stringify), so 1 vs "1" and true vs "true" are distinct classes and a row cannot be miscounted as covering both (no false 100%). F2 fix: a present constraints list is validated like rows (array of non-empty objects, declared factors and values) and fails closed otherwise, instead of being silently ignored.

boundary.evidence: a reference tested oracle (the worked example of the rule); single purpose.

ownership.evidence: the leak-detection logic has one owner; the rule it illustrates is documented once in SKILL.md Step 6.

dependency.evidence: Node built-ins only; no outbound web.

error-handling.evidence: fail-closed on no secret, an unreadable file, and (F4 fix) ANY secret that normalizes to zero tokens even when mixed with a usable one, so an unchecked secret never reads as clean. F3 fix: the whole-token model's limit (a secret embedded inside a larger alphanumeric token is not caught) is now named in the script header, SKILL.md, the ADR, and the CHANGELOG, and pinned by a characterization test.

boundary.evidence: integration tests; spawn the real scripts.

error-handling.evidence: discriminating (a no-op script flips the partial-grid / variant-leak cases); extended with the F1 type-collision, F2 constraint-validation, F4 unusable-secret, and F3 embedded-limit regression cases. 32 pass.

boundary.evidence: the two @audience:agent scenarios drive the real coverage-measure.mjs and leak-check.mjs; a hand-picked grid measures short while a covering array measures full, and the checker catches the variant and ignores the substring where a naive check gets both wrong.

dependency.evidence: Node built-ins; spawns the real scripts.

error-handling.evidence: assertions throw on a wrong exit; no step-text collision with existing step files. 15/15 scenarios pass.

boundary.evidence: documentation of the two rules and the ownership split (oracle rule here, cross-ref to verifiable-quality-gates).

ownership.evidence: one owner each; cross-referenced, not duplicated.

error-handling.evidence: F3 fix: the leak-check embedded-secret limit is named in the ADR Consequences, SKILL.md Step 6, and the CHANGELOG. F5 fix: combinatorial-testing.md now cites the real Step 6 phrase ("Trust only a tested checker (the oracle rule)"). NIST SP 800-142 claims are paraphrased and hedged, not overstated.

findings.finding: values that stringify alike (1 vs "1", true vs "true") collapsed to one coverage key, so a row covering one counted as covering both - a false 100% / exit 0, a silent pass in a tool whose exit code is the evidence.
findings.resolution: fixed: the key JSON.stringifies each value, keeping distinct value classes distinct. Regression tests added.

findings.finding: constraints bypassed the fail-closed validation that rows get: a non-array constraints value, a non-object element, or an undeclared factor/value was silently ignored, dropping an intended exclusion or (if over-broad) shrinking the denominator to a false exit 0.
findings.resolution: fixed: a present constraints list is validated as an array of non-empty objects over declared factors and values, failing closed otherwise. Regression tests added.

findings.finding: the whole-token model misses a secret embedded inside a larger alphanumeric token (a concatenated machine secret / API key), and the named limits did not say so - a gap in the skill's own name-your-limits discipline.
findings.resolution: fixed (documentation): the limit is named in the script header, SKILL.md Step 6, the ADR Consequences, and the CHANGELOG, and pinned by a characterization test. The whole-token model is kept (it is correct for the audit's human-readable-secret cases); machine secrets are directed to a substring/entropy check.

findings.finding: a secret that normalized to zero tokens was silently dropped when mixed with a usable secret, and the run still reported clean, so a secret the caller asked to check went unchecked with no signal.
findings.resolution: fixed: ANY secret that normalizes to zero tokens now fails closed (exit 2), naming the dropped secret(s). Regression test added.

findings.finding: the reference cited a SKILL.md phrase ("Test the checker before you trust its 0-found") that does not exist, so the pointer led nowhere.
findings.resolution: fixed: it now cites the real Step 6 heading phrase.
